article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: Screwdriver OG × California Indica × Gorilla Glue × Maple Leaf Indica
Breeder: Sensi Seeds
THC Content: 20.3%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: limonene , myrcene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sweet orange, lemon zest, earthy hashish
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 460–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 750 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Good cannabis flower can be recognized by its fragrance, but Sticky Orange makes its first impression through texture and color. Its dense buds carry an unusually heavy coating of resin, surrounded by fiery orange pistils that can nearly conceal the green flower beneath them. The aroma is equally distinctive, blending freshly peeled citrus with the darker qualities of aged hashish, warm spice, and earth.

Developed by Sensi Seeds, this productive indica-dominant marijuana strain brings together genetics associated with California cannabis, traditional Afghan hash plants, and influential Skunk and Gorilla Glue breeding lines. What began as Sticky Orange XXL Automatic later expanded into a feminized photoperiod version, allowing the breeder to explore the same general characteristics through different growing formats. Behind the bright name lies a remarkably physical experience, considerable flower density, and a genetic background that connects several important chapters of modern cannabis history.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic story begins with Sensi Seeds’ original Sticky Orange XXL Automatic, an indica-dominant hybrid combining California Indica, Shiva Skunk , Gorilla Glue, and Maple Leaf Indica. Each contributes a recognizable part of the cultivar’s character. California Indica connects the breeding line to the West Coast Orange Bud tradition and Afghan hash-plant influences, bringing citrus character alongside sturdy, productive growth. Shiva Skunk originates from Northern Lights #5 crossed with Skunk #1 , two foundational varieties in Dutch cannabis breeding. Their influence reinforces resin production, compact flower formation, and the powerful physical qualities associated with traditional indica hybrids. Gorilla Glue, widely associated with GG4, adds modern American genetics descended from Chem’s Sister, Sour Dubb, and Chocolate Diesel . Maple Leaf Indica completes the older genetic foundation with Afghan-derived characteristics valued for heavy resin production and deeply relaxing effects.

The newer Sticky Orange XXL Feminized, introduced for Sensi Seeds’ 2026 catalog, has a more specifically documented four-parent arrangement: (Screwdriver OG × California Indica) × (Gorilla Glue × Maple Leaf Indica). Screwdriver OG introduces additional citrus-oriented genetics associated with Purple Punch and Clementine , reinforcing the strain family’s orange character. This distinction matters because the photoperiod and automatic releases should not be treated as genetically identical simply because they share a name. The feminized version is classified as approximately 75% indica, compared with 80% for the automatic. Both preserve the broader objective of combining old-school hashish qualities with modern resin-rich American hybrids, but their growth cycles, structures, and exact pedigrees differ.
Effects and Experience

Sticky Orange develops its effects around physical relaxation rather than intense mental stimulation. The initial sensation is generally described as gentle and progressively calming, beginning with a reduction in perceived tension before becoming more noticeable throughout the body. Instead of a sudden rush of cerebral energy, many of the characteristics emphasized by Sensi Seeds involve quiet comfort, a settled mood, and an increasingly relaxed physical state. The psychological experience may remain relatively clear during the early stages, although THC can still impair attention, memory, judgment, and reaction time. Its indica-oriented character makes the cultivar more naturally associated with quiet recreational periods than demanding activities.

As intoxication develops, the physical component can become considerably stronger. Larger amounts may produce pronounced heaviness, reduced motivation for movement, and a preference for remaining seated. The breeder describes the effects as both intense and relatively long-lasting, particularly in the newer photoperiod release. A documented autoflowering harvest produced a laboratory THC result of 20.3%, demonstrating substantial potency in that specific sample, although the figure cannot reliably predict every future harvest. Sensitivity varies widely between individuals, and high-THC cannabis can cause dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, anxiety, impaired coordination, or temporary cognitive difficulties. Its gradual onset should not encourage rapid repeated consumption before the full effects become apparent.
Medical Benefits

The physically calming qualities of Sticky Orange may interest medical marijuana consumers exploring cannabis for persistent discomfort, muscle tension, and temporary relief from stress-related symptoms. THC acts on cannabinoid receptors throughout the nervous system, influencing mechanisms involved in pain perception, appetite, sensory processing, and emotional responses. Research involving certain standardized cannabis-based medicines has demonstrated modest benefits for some chronic pain conditions, particularly selected forms of neuropathic pain. However, results differ between formulations, and evidence from clinical trials involving specific medicines cannot automatically be applied to an individual marijuana strain. No controlled clinical studies have established Sticky Orange as an effective treatment for a particular medical condition.

Sedating effects may become relevant for adults who experience difficulty unwinding, although relaxation and improved sleep quality are not necessarily the same outcome. Repeated THC consumption can produce tolerance, change sleep patterns, and cause sleep disturbances after discontinuation. Cannabis can also increase anxiety or produce uncomfortable psychological effects in susceptible individuals, even when a variety is generally described as calming. Potential interactions with sedatives and other prescription medications require particular consideration. Medical consumers should prioritize laboratory-tested cannabinoid information and professional guidance rather than relying on strain names or recreational descriptions to determine suitability.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The flavor profile contains an interesting surprise: despite its orange-focused name, Sticky Orange is not exclusively an orange-flavored marijuana variety. Sensi Seeds describes an unmistakable citrus opening, with freshly peeled lemon zest providing much of the brightness in the original autoflowering release. The newer photoperiod version emphasizes sweet orange candy and a resinous Kush character, sometimes accompanied by a faint diesel-like sharpness. Beneath the fruit notes lies an old-fashioned combination of earthy hashish and warm spice. These darker characteristics distinguish the cultivar from modern orange strains that lean heavily toward sweet mandarin or tropical candy. Its fragrance can be relatively restrained during early growth before developing greater complexity as the flowers mature and cure.

Terpene chemistry may help explain some of these contrasts, although detailed batch-specific laboratory profiles are needed to establish the dominant compounds. Limonene is a plausible contributor to the citrus impression, while myrcene may introduce earthy or herbal depth. Beta-caryophyllene could account for some of the peppery warmth, and additional volatile compounds may contribute hashish, diesel, or chocolate-like nuances. These associations are not proof of a particular terpene’s abundance in the finished flower. On the palate, bright citrus generally appears first, followed by earthy sweetness, spice, and a faint cocoa-like finish. Proper drying and curing are particularly important for preserving the separation between delicate citrus aromatics and the heavier underlying fragrance.
Growing Information

Compact architecture and substantial flower production are central to the appeal of the original Sticky Orange XXL Automatic. Sensi Seeds describes plants generally reaching approximately 70–100 centimeters indoors, with thicker branches, dark green foliage, and closely arranged flowering sites. As flowering progresses, dense clusters develop into substantial colas covered with trichomes and bright orange pistils. Purple tones may appear in the foliage toward maturity, creating additional contrast against the resin-covered buds. The automatic version begins flowering without a required change in daylight duration, making it approachable for beginners. Its advertised flowering stage lasts approximately 45–50 days, although the complete life cycle includes vegetative development and may take considerably longer. In one documented Sensi Seeds cultivation report, the plant finished after 94 days from the beginning of the grow, with 73 days recorded in the flowering phase.

The 2026 feminized photoperiod release offers greater flexibility over vegetative development and final plant size. Indoor specimens are described as reaching approximately 70–110 centimeters, developing a strong central stem with numerous productive lateral branches. Outdoors, favorable conditions may allow heights approaching two meters. One particularly useful characteristic is its relatively slow vegetative growth combined with tight internodal spacing and substantial secondary flower production. Sensi Seeds identifies approximately 55–60 days as the photoperiod flowering period, with indoor yields potentially reaching 460–650 grams per square meter. Outdoor plants may produce as much as 750 grams each under optimal conditions. The breeder considers the variety well suited to relatively simple canopy arrangements, while dense lower growth may benefit from selective removal to improve air movement and concentrate development on productive flowering sites.

Both versions produce exceptionally resinous flowers, making post-harvest handling an important part of preserving quality. Trichome coverage can become so pronounced that mature buds develop a greasy, tacky surface, while orange pistils give the flower an almost golden appearance from a distance. Adequate ventilation and humidity management are important because dense buds can retain moisture and become vulnerable to fungal problems. The autoflowering version is particularly associated with temperate and continental climates, whereas the photoperiod release favors warmer, sunny conditions with a sufficiently long growing season. Outdoor photoperiod harvest generally takes place during autumn, while automatic plants mature according to their individual development cycle rather than a fixed seasonal date. Stable growing conditions, careful harvest timing, and controlled curing help preserve the cultivar’s high resin content, attractive coloration, and distinctive citrus-hashish aroma.
FAQ
Is Sticky Orange an indica or sativa strain?

Sticky Orange is an indica-dominant cannabis hybrid developed by Sensi Seeds. The original XXL Automatic version is classified as approximately 80% indica and 20% sativa, while the newer feminized photoperiod release is approximately 75% indica. Both are associated with pronounced physical relaxation and dense, resinous flowers.
What are the genetics of Sticky Orange?

The original autoflowering version combines California Indica, Shiva Skunk, Gorilla Glue, and Maple Leaf Indica. The 2026 feminized photoperiod release has a more specific pedigree of (Screwdriver OG × California Indica) × (Gorilla Glue × Maple Leaf Indica). These versions share important genetic influences but are not described through identical parentage.
How strong is Sticky Orange weed?

Sticky Orange is a THC-dominant marijuana variety with potentially powerful physical effects. A documented cultivation report for the autoflowering version recorded 20.3% THC in the harvested flower. However, potency varies by phenotype, cultivation conditions, and processing. The breeder has not established a universal THC concentration applicable to every release and harvest.
What does Sticky Orange taste and smell like?

Its aromatic profile combines sweet orange, lemon zest, earthy hashish, warm spice, and subtle chocolate. The photoperiod version may emphasize orange candy and faint diesel undertones, while the original autoflowering release is particularly associated with lemon zest, earth, and traditional hashish qualities.
How long does Sticky Orange take to flower?

Sticky Orange XXL Feminized has a breeder-listed flowering period of approximately 55–60 days. Sticky Orange XXL Automatic is advertised with a flowering period around 45–50 days, although the complete seed-to-harvest cycle takes longer and actual plants may require additional time. The automatic version flowers independently of the light cycle, unlike the photoperiod release.
Final Thoughts on Sticky Orange

Sticky Orange occupies an interesting position between traditional indica breeding and modern high-resin cannabis genetics. Its heritage combines the earthy depth of Afghan-derived varieties, the structural reliability of classic Skunk and California lines, and the sticky flower characteristics associated with Gorilla Glue. Rather than offering an uncomplicated orange-candy experience, the cultivar delivers a more layered aromatic identity involving fresh citrus, warm spice, aged hashish, and occasional chocolate or diesel notes.

Sensi Seeds’ decision to offer both autoflowering and feminized photoperiod versions expands the appeal of this productive marijuana family while preserving its recognizable characteristics. The original automatic provides relatively compact, uncomplicated growth, whereas the newer photoperiod release allows greater control over plant development and potentially larger harvests. For cannabis enthusiasts who appreciate dense flowers, vivid orange pistils, substantial resin production, and deeply relaxing effects, Sticky Orange represents a distinctive combination of established genetic heritage and modern breeding priorities.
